h: Make a science weekend of Newcastle
p: Newcastle is a brilliant city for curious families, and some of its best science stops are a stone's throw from the Centre for Life. Just behind it, at Blandford Square, the Discovery Museum tells the story of Tyneside's inventors and industries, and it's free to visit. Its star exhibit is Turbinia, the steam turbine ship that astonished the world with its speed in the 1890s. It's a real head-turner.

Across the city centre, near the universities, the Great North Museum: Hancock is another free favourite, with natural history, ancient Egypt, a model of Hadrian's Wall and a life-size T. rex skeleton cast that stops kids in their tracks. It has its own planetarium too, so space fans can make a double-header of it.

Down on the Quayside, the Gateshead Millennium Bridge tilts to let boats pass, earning it the nickname the Blinking Eye. Across it you'll find BALTIC, a contemporary art centre in a converted flour mill, and The Glasshouse International Centre for Music in its curved glass building. A little further afield, the Angel of the North stands over the A1 in Gateshead, well worth a stop if you're driving.

For the Life Science Centre itself, allow at least a few hours, and longer if a big touring exhibition is on. The Wow Zone tends to be noisiest, so tackle it when the kids need to let off steam and save the calmer labs for later.
